dedupe_keys.name: barbados coastal zone management unit oceanographic buoys

description: The Coastal Zone Management Unit of Barbados installed three oceanographic buoys in deep water (more than 80 metres) off the south, east and north coasts as an output of its Coastal Risk Assessment and Management Programme. The buoys give the unit the data it needs to model how open-ocean waves and currents translate into the wave and current patterns seen near the shore, so that it can better understand beach erosion and accretion and make beach protection and restoration work more effective. They measure wave height and direction, current speed and direction, wind speed and direction and sea water temperature, and the page links to the data of each buoy: North Point and Conset Bay are marked currently inactive, and South Point is active. The same site lists sea level stations, a reef health index and the coastal infrastructure programme. Access to the buoy data links is free; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: two of the three buoys are inactive, and the archive length is not given on the page. Coverage is the coast of Barbados. It supports coastal hazard exposure analysis and the design of coastal defences and nature-based beach protection; related records are the Danish Kystdata coastal measurements and the CEREMA national coastal erosion indicator.
